title: The NYT Cooking app is testing AI recipe modifications

claims.claim: The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes.

evidence.quote: The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes
The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes, and it’s sparked some drama among users.

claims.claim: NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko announced the new AI feature last Friday.

evidence.quote: NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko announced the feature last Friday

claims.claim: Customized recipes are private and can't be published or shared via the app.

evidence.quote: Customized recipes are private and can’t be published or shared via the app.

claims.claim: The AI modification feature is currently available to all Cooking subscribers on the iOS app.

evidence.quote: it’s currently available to all Cooking subscribers on the iOS app
it’s currently available to all Cooking subscribers on the iOS app, and will be more broadly available “soon.”

claims.claim: Genevieve Ko stated that there is currently no way to disable the AI feature.

evidence.quote: When one user asked if there will be a way to disable the AI feature, Ko responded with “No, not at this time,”
When one user asked if there will be a way to disable the AI feature, Ko responded with “No, not at this time,” and noted that the feature is “completely optional to use.”

claims.claim: AI was previously used by the NYT Cooking app to convert imperial volume measurements to metric weight measurements two years ago.

evidence.quote: Ko says it was used to convert imperial volume measurements to metric weight measurements in recipes two years ago

claims.claim: A feature was added last year that converts recipes to halve or double the original serving size.

evidence.quote: a feature was added last year that converts recipes to halve or double the original serving size.

claims.claim: NYT spokesperson Jordan Cohen stated that comments on the article remained open for four days.

evidence.quote: NYT spokesperson Jordan Cohen tells The Verge that this is standard practice: “Comments on this article remained open for four days

NYT spokesperson Jordan Cohen tells The Verge that this is standard practice: “Comments on this article remained open for four days, with editors from Cooking taking care to answer questions, address concerns and engage directly with readers.
